the morphology of PVDF microfiltration membranes is significantly affected by the type of solvent used in the casting solution and the thickness of the casting solution.
the solvent type and the polymer concentration in the casting solution significantly affect the morphology and the performance of PVDF microfiltration membranes.
the PVDF microfiltration membranes were successfully fabricated by the phase inversion method.

the development of a novel membrane for the treatment of oily wastewaters.
the development of new PVDF membrane materials for use in microfiltration and ultrafiltration applications.
the effect of the preparation influencing parameters on membrane morphology and permeate flux.

the solvent type and its concentration play a major role in determining the morphology of the membrane and hence the membrane performance.
the solvent type has an important effect on the membrane structure and permeate flux.
the type of solvent used for membrane preparation plays an important role in the membrane performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the membrane performance is strongly influenced by the solvent used.
solvent selection has a significant effect on membrane performance.
the solvent and nonsolvenr interaction is the main parameter affecting the membrane morphology and performance.

the use of a solvent that has the closest solubility parameters to the nonsolvent is the key to obtaining the highest permeate flux and the best membrane morphology.
